one_liner: Families share photo albums through an invite link and get a weekly email digest of new photos.
bullets: Anyone holding the album link can view AND upload, with no per-person identity.
Uploads go browser-to-storage via presigned URLs; a worker does thumbnails, HEIC and GPS stripping.
Weekly digest is sent Monday 08:00 local time by an hourly scheduler job.
Three privacy-relevant gaps are open: link revocation, leaving members' photos, file retention.
MVP scope: P1 is albums, uploads and invites; the digest (P2) can ship later.
you_must_decide: Do invite links expire or become revocable, given they grant upload rights?
What happens to a member's photos when they leave the album?
How long are original files retained, and what is the storage budget per family?

decisions.title: Permanent invite link with full member rights
decisions.choice: One permanent token per album; anyone with the link can view and upload.
decisions.risk: A leaked link exposes family photos and lets strangers upload; there is no way to revoke it.

decisions.title: Direct-to-storage uploads
decisions.choice: Browser uploads to object storage with presigned URLs.
decisions.rationale: Keeps 25 MB files off the API and meets the 30 s upload goal.
decisions.risk: No resumable uploads: large HEIC files on weak mobile connections may fail and restart.

decisions.title: GPS stripped only before other members see the photo
decisions.choice: Originals are kept with EXIF; GPS is removed in the worker before photos are visible.
decisions.rationale: Privacy for shared photos while keeping the original file.
decisions.risk: Originals with location data are stored indefinitely while retention is undefined.

decisions.title: HEIC converted to JPEG in the worker
decisions.choice: Convert server-side and keep the original.

decisions.title: Timezone-aware digest via hourly job
decisions.choice: Celery beat runs hourly and sends to members whose local time is Monday 08:00.
decisions.rationale: Respects timezones without one scheduled job per user.
decisions.risk: Members with half-hour offsets (e.g. India) never match an exact hour boundary.

risks.title: Abuse through open upload links
risks.impact: Anyone with the link can upload arbitrary content to a family album; no moderation or removal flow is specified.
risks.mitigation: Add link revocation and owner-side photo deletion to P1.

risks.title: Storage cost is unbounded
risks.impact: Originals plus converted copies, 25 MB each, with no retention period or budget.
risks.mitigation: Decide retention and a per-family quota before launch.

risks.title: Success metric SC-002 is only tested at the end
risks.impact: The 30 s upload goal drives the architecture but is verified only in the final polish phase.
risks.mitigation: Run a throttled upload spike right after T009.

questions.question: How are duplicate uploads detected and handled?
questions.why_it_matters: Listed as an edge case but no requirement or task covers it; families often upload the same photo twice.

questions.question: Can the owner delete photos uploaded by others?
questions.why_it_matters: With open upload links, the owner needs a way to remove unwanted content; no requirement says so.

questions.question: Can members opt out of the weekly digest?
questions.why_it_matters: FR-005 makes it mandatory; unsubscribe is usually a legal requirement for recurring email.
